The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

The atmosphere is building. 🇮🇩📈 pic.twitter.com/fhXfDVAf6s

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#2163. Fabregas si inchina a Chivu, quest'Inter è (ancora) troppo forte per il Como

L'Inter torna a vincere in campionato e lo fa con una prova di forza contro il Como di Cesc Fabregas. A San Siro finisce 2-0, con i nerazzurri capaci di indirizzare la sfida già nei primi venti minuti grazie alle reti di Pio Esposito e Marcus Thuram. L'approccio della squadra di Cristian Chivu è praticamente perfetto: pressing alto, intensità e grande aggressività impediscono ai lariani di sviluppare il consueto gioco di possesso. Al 12' è il giovane centravanti italiano a sbloccare il risultato, finalizzando il cross di Spence dopo una bella combinazione con Thuram. Sette minuti più tardi arriva il raddoppio del francese, bravo ad approfittare di una respinta imprecisa di Valle sul cross di Zielinski. Nella ripresa Fabregas prova a correre ai ripari con alcuni cambi, ma l'Inter continua a controllare la partita e sfiora più volte il tris, soprattutto con Dimarco e Thuram. Il Como ha un sussulto intorno all'ora di gioco con Nico Paz, che costringe Martinez a un grande intervento, e prova a rendersi pericoloso nel finale, senza però trovare la via della rete. Per Chivu arrivano tre punti pesanti e una risposta convincente dopo la sconfitta nel derby: i nerazzurri si portano così a una sola lunghezza dalla Lazio capolista.

"Partirei dalle 9 partite in 27 giorni, superate con energia seppur con alti e bassi. Si cerca sempre di fare meglio ma a volte ci sono anche delle amarezze che vanno accettate e ingoiate. Basta prepararsi bene col lavoro e la mentalità alle partite successive. Oggi abbiamo alzato il ritmo e l'intensità abbiamo trovato la nostra preparazione dal punto di vista della qualità e delle pressioni, si è ragionato di squadra. Un primo tempo fatto bene sotto tutti i punti di vista che ci ha permesso di andare all'intervallo sopra di due gol, poi a volte serve saper gestire le energie e i momenti della partita. Faccio i complimenti ai ragazzi che oggi sono stati meravigliosi".

"Oggi possiamo dire tante cose, ma l'Inter è stata molto meglio di noi, ha dimostrato di essere ad un livello superiore. Dobbiamo accettarlo, ci riguarderemo la partita perché tutti devono capire come abbiamo perso questa partita. Fa parte del nostro processo di crescita, sono 3 punti che cambiano poco perché essere a questo punto della stagione 4-5-6 punti dietro il quarto posto non cambia nulla e lo scorso anno lo dimostra. Abbiamo perso contro uno squadrone e speriamo un giorno di avere l'opportunità di vincere".

#2161. 19-year-old Southampton starlet showcasing exciting potential in European loan after early transfer interest

Southampton sent eight players out on loan this campaign. With a mixture of academy talents and players who are on their way out of St Mary’s, the Saints are seeing mixed success from the departed members of the squad.

Moses Sesay, Nicholas Oyekunle and Jay Robinson were the three teenagers to leave for the season. It’s the latter who Tonda Eckert will be monitoring closely after a breakout term last year in the Championship.

Robinson made 28 appearances for Southampton, scoring twice and providing an assist. Minutes were always going to be hard to come by for the 19-year-old this season. With a move to Monza secured, the attacker has plenty to prove in the Serie A.

Securing a loan move to Serie A is a positive sign of how much potential Robinson has to unlock. It’s safe to say that despite a slow start to life at Monza, the 19-year-old is becoming a key player for the Italian outfit.

The Southampton academy graduate had to wait until September to make his first start, and he impressed in a 1-0 win against Torino. Featuring in an attacking midfield role, he completed the most dribbles in the game with four and had nine touches inside the opposition’s box.

His first goal came in the next match, in which he completed 78% of his passes and was dispossessed only once. Former Saints boss Ivan Juric has shown full faith in Robinson, starting the teenager in three of the last four outings.

The 19-year-old’s best display came against Cagliari, where he scored once in a 4-0 win. Two out of his three dribbles were successful in the game, and he made three line-breaking passes. It has been an impressive loan stint for the youngster with Inter Milan registering their interest.

Southampton have the option to recall Robinson from his loan spell in January. However, given his promising spell so far, the Saints would be reckless to do so.

At left-wing, the South Coast outfit currently have the options of Leo Scienza and Sam Edozie, as well as Lewis Dobbin, who can play there too. Edozie is likely to depart in January, though, after putting in a transfer request late in the summer window.

This would ultimately leave Eckert’s side short of attackers in that position. However, they must avoid recalling Robinson to improve their depth. Even if Edozie were to leave, his exit would give Dobbin a better chance of breaking into the first team after just 409 minutes played.

Most importantly, it would do no favours to the 19-year-old’s development. The Southampton prospect has only recently become settled at Monza, and with his minutes increasing over the last couple of months, the South Coast outfit can’t afford to ruin his crucial playing time.

#2160. Fiorentina due volte avanti e due volte ripresa dalla Juventus. Spalletti duro nel post match

In un Franchi agghindato per le grandi occasioni, la Fiorentina e Juventus danno vita ad un match di box in cui alla fine nessuno dei due pugili va al tappeto. Il primo destro lo tira la squadra di Vanoli, che trova il vantaggio con Pellegrino; Spalletti risponde con il montante di Woltemade che vale il pareggio. Padroni di casa ancora avanti ad inizio ripresa con il terzo gol consecutivo di Njie ma di nuovo riacciuffati da Bremer.

In un Franchi infuocato, trascinato da una spettacolare coreografia, la Fiorentina parte subito con il piede sull’acceleratore e trova il vantaggio dopo appena quattro minuti con Mateo Pellegrino. L’argentino, sugli sviluppi di un corner battuto perfettamente da Gonçalves, svetta sul secondo palo e firma il suo quinto gol stagionale, celebrato con la mitraglia in omaggio a Batistuta. La Juventus, però, non si lascia intimorire e con il passare dei minuti prende in mano il controllo del gioco, trovando il pareggio al 31’ con Woltemade, bravo a sfruttare l’assist di Kolo Muani. I bianconeri sfiorano anche il sorpasso prima dell’intervallo, ma De Gea e la difesa viola riescono a evitare il peggio. Nella ripresa la Fiorentina riparte forte e al 54’ torna avanti grazie a Njie, il più rapido a ribadire in rete un pallone rimasto in area dopo il cross di Jimenez. La reazione della Juventus, però, non tarda ad arrivare: al 66’ Bremer svetta su tutti sugli sviluppi di un calcio d’angolo e batte De Gea, ristabilendo nuovamente la parità. Nel finale i viola trovano anche la rete del possibile 3-2 con Dragusin, ma l’arbitro annulla per una spinta ai danni di Bremer. Nei minuti di recupero entrambe le squadre hanno l'occasione per portare a casa l'intera posta in palio: Kolo Muani si fa fermare da Fagioli a tu per tu con il portiere, mentre sul ribaltamento di fronte Mastantuono sfiora il gol vittoria, trovando però la risposta decisiva di Vicario. Al Franchi finisce così in parità, al termine di una sfida intensa, ricca di occasioni e colpi di scena.

Clicca qui per le pagelle di Fiorentina-Juventus a cura di TMW.

Ha fatto discutere anche la direzione di gara di Andrea Colombo. La prima per un possibile rosso a Oulai: il centrocampista viola, ammonito al 51', rischia grosso pochi secondi dopo per un fallo a centrocampo su Boga. Colombo non lo punisce, decisione che sembra corretta ma che non fa felice Spalletti. Ben più fondate le proteste bianconere al 79': Joao Mario tocca il pallone in area col braccio, Colombo lascia correre ed il VAR interpreta il pallone come "inaspettato" (Car Di Paolo, Avar Meraviglia), ma la sensazione è che fosse calcio di rigore per la Juventus al di là delle interpretazioni. Quindi gol annullato alla Fiorentina con Dragusin: Colombo non ha dubbi e punisce giustamente la spinta del difensore viola su Bremer.

Un pareggio che in conferenza stampa, il tecnico della Fiorentina Paolo Vanoli ha commentato così sui tanti gol presi: “Ci stiamo lavorando e ci dobbiamo lavorare, migliorando le qualità individuali. Questa squadra deve proporre gioco, non è il momento di aver paura dei tanti gol presi. Serve migliorare col possesso ed essere più scaltri in certe occasioni. Questo fa parte della costruzione di una squadra che ha davanti un futuro importante. È un aspetto su cui serve lavorare perché due gol a partita sono tanti ma mi prendo i piccoli passi: siamo andati in vantaggio e siamo andati ancora vicini alla vittoria contro una squadra forte come la Juve. Stasera sono arrabbiato perché andava portata a casa. Ai ragazzi ho detto: dovete andare a casa ed essere incazzati perché serve salire di livello. Due punti persi? Per me sì. Dobbiamo essere arrabbiati più di altre partite perché abbiamo fatto una prestazione di coraggio e qualità. Potevamo servire meglio gli attaccanti ma si deve essere arrabbiati per due punti diversi. La maglia però è stata onorata".

Queste invece l’analisi del tecnico della Juventus Luciano Spalletti: “Non sono contentissimo perché non esprimiamo un livello di calcio costante degno di poter aspirare a qualcosa di importante. Ci sono momenti in cui ci siamo, poi ad un certo punto molliamo, perdiamo palloni facili da leggere, perdiamo di equilibrio. Poi potevamo anche vincere la partita, abbiamo avuto le occasioni per farlo. Abbiamo questa alternanza che non mi fa essere contento. Perché poi la squadra ha anche messo voglia, così come la Fiorentina. È stata una partita a chi se le dava più forte, però poi non siamo continui". Poi l’elogio a Kolo Muani: “Ora abbiamo il Kolo Muani che desideravamo avere e non conta quella che è la posizione perché quando decide di fare le cose con forza con la qualità di corsa che ha lo puoi mettere da qualsiasi parte. Può giocare attaccante, ala, ma fino ad ora aveva avuto un livello un pochino inferiore".

#2159. Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount

Michael Carrick said he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

“It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”

“We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have big season and hope to win a trophy.”

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Two things to worry about, however, were the early exits of Mason Mount and Tom Heaton with injuries. They’ll especially hope the Mount knock isn’t anything mid or long term.

Nearly done and it’s been a good run out for United. They’ve looked the better, sharper side and, if anything, deserve to win. In mitigation, this is United fourth pre-season game to PSG’s second...

Fernandes has one thing on his mind when he gets the ball 25 yards out in the centre of the park - a shot. He unleashes the attempt, destined for the bottom-left corner, forcing Longoni, the sub goalkeeper, into a good save.

Two chances for United in quick succession. A lovely ball from the middle of the park by Zirkzee finds Dalot on the right. He chips the ball to the back post where one of the Fletchers (sorry, I am not sure which) heads for goal. His attempt is blocked and the ball, ultimately, falls at the feet of Lacey whose shot is blazed high over the bar.

There have been plenty of good things for Carrick to take from this match. The passing, while not of the standard of a cut-and-thrust Premier League match, has been good for the time of year, and there have been enough flashes of brilliance/class/invention etc to suggest that pre-season is moving in the right direction.

Lovely bit of play by United. A great pass with the outside of the boot from the inside-left channel by Tielemans finds Fernandes who plays a sidefooted shot that goes just wide.

Tielemans’s first bit of brilliance from the Belgian there.

Both sides losing possession a fair bit at the moment. Strong pre-season vibes right now.

Maguire has had a good game. He’s played a number of long passes from the back and looked assured. This time he’s up in the PSG half and decides to have a pop - his shot testing Safanov, who saves well.

Had there been VAR Safanov might have had something to answer for...he may have beaten Zirkzee to the ball but he flew in the air and jurt the United man in the process.

Anwway, there’s no VAR (hurrah, for those of you who consider it a modern-day evil) and it doesn’t matter.

Chance for United to go ahead and it comes from two things. (i) A long, hopeful ball from Fernandes that looks for Zirkzee (ii) Safanov rushing off his line and into no-man’s land. The ball comes loose and Jack Fletcher, instead of having a go at goal, with the keeper on the ground and out of the game, passes to Lacey whose shot is wide.

Tyler Fletcher loses the ball near the United half and it, ultimately, results in a PSG corner. From the set piece United defend well and snuff out all hint of danger.

PSG seeing more of the ball at the moment. They work the ball to the right and Amass brings down Mbaye.

From the resulting free-kick, in the final third, the French side whip in the ball but Mee is up ot the challenge and come to collect well.

Santos, Mbeumo, Shaw, Amad, Lacey are off

Fernandes, Jack Feltcher, Zirkzee and Amass are on.

A raft of changes for PSG sees Marquinhos and João Neves, among others, come on. More like it, in terms of first-team ‘names’, on the pitch for the European Cup champions.

United on top in this half, as they were in the first.

The paces quickens and the game is much better for it. Mbuemo drives toward the PSG box, he cuts inside from the right before unleashing a shot that is bound for the back of the net before a fine one-handed save by Safanov. Credit, too, for Maguire whose long ball from the back found Mbuemo brilliantly. Promising...

Lacey tries to play in Dorgu on the left but he’s asking too much of his team-mate. Wonder when the expected raft of changes will take place?

Slow start to the second half. This is very much pre-season-friendly pace.

Having seen Mount limp off in the first half, there’s more worry at the start of the second and Heaton is force off with what looks like a hamstrung injury. He dashed off his line to clear a ball and in doing so has tweaked something. Mee replaces him.

Back under way Gothenburg - there have been a number of changes and will bring them to you once I’ve worked out who has come on and who they’ve replaced.

A world record that still stands...(this was back in 1995).

And that is it for the first 45 minutes. PSG took the early lead, but from that moment on United have been the better side and deservedly are level through Mbueno’s goal.

There will be one minute of added time at the end of what has been a good first half for Man Utd.

Amad has a go from outside the box forcing the save from Safanov. He’s such a live wire and one of the best in his position in the top flight. Him or Antony? No contest, strange it took United a while to work that one out.

Yet more good work from the underrated Amad. He again closes down well on the right before winning back possession and cutting the ball back for Lacey. To think he was starring for Sunderland in the Championship while Antony was starting for United...

United have been the better side since conceding earlier and, as if to illustrate my point, as I typed that an Mbuemo free-kick is well saved by Safanov. That was heading for the top-right bin.

Great work on the left by Dorgu and Shaw ends with the latter chipping the ball to the back post where Amad is lurking with intent. The Ivorian looks to head the ball home, but before he can get anything on it it looks as though he’s pushed in the back. United players are sure it’s a penalty but, more importantly, the referee doesn’t.

Amad does brilliantly, winning the ball off Koukaba in the final third, from there he scampers toward the box before playing in Mbuemo who takes one touch before firing in a shot into the bottom right corner of the net.

Free-kick for PSG on the right, near the final third. The ball comes in and it’s straight into the arms of Heaton in the United goal.

Kvaratskhelia, not seen much of him so far, runs into the box, but Amad does well to usher him back out.

The match is pedestrian at the moment, but as I type that, Dorgu, yep, him again, drives down the left and puts in a good cross that is well intercepted by Safanov in the PSG goal.

United continue to see more of the ball, Dorgu’s seeing more of it than most. But, no chances really fashioned, still, plenty of time to go.

Worry for United having to sub off Mount. It looks as though he took a knock to a foot and Carrick and co will hope it’s not a long-term injury. Mount, who’s had a good pre-season, has been replaced by Fletcher, son of Darren.

Foul on Mazraoui results in two things. The Mount has to come off, and, United have a free-kick on the edge of the PSG area.

From the set-piece Mbuemo has a go and it’s a regulation save from Safonov in the PSG goal.

Heaven loses possession in the middle of the park and from there it’s like the parting of the Red Sea as PSG have a three-on-one. Mbaye gets the shot in on goal but Andrey Santos covers back brilliantly and does enough to get something on the ball. He’s started both this match and pre-season well.

United are looking half decent on the ball. They’re passing it well and not afraid to switch things around.

A lovely long ball from Maguire finds Dorgo whose lovely first touch takes him into the box before a cut back is intercepted by a PSG man. Promising signs though for Carrick’s men.

United seeing more of the ball at the moment. They’re being patient but cannot fashion an opening and the ball is worked all the way back to Heaton in goal.

Needless to say this is being played at a slowish pace...no blood-and-guts challenges being put in.

Good work down the right sees Amad plays in Shay Lacey who crosses into the box. The ball find shte head of Mbuemo and the ball sails over the bar. Better from United.

United started slowly against Atletico and they’ve done the same here.

Bright start to say the least from the French side. They work the ball left and it’s an easy cross from Dro Fernandez for Mbaye to tap home for the very early lead.

They’re under way in Sweden. United are in their new vibrant red kit and PSG in their blue, red and white kit. Big fan of the French side’s kit, it harks back to the kit they had in the 1990s when the likes of George Weah and David Ginola were entertaining in the capital of France.

Man Utd: Heaton, Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw, Mount, Santos, Dorgu, Lacey, Amad, Mbeumo; Subs: Heath, Mee, Amass, Armer, Dalot, Yoro, Fernandes, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Tielemans, Zirkzee

Paris St-Germain: Safonov, Pacho, Zabarnyi, Koukaba, Boly, Beraldo, Dro, Mayulu, Kvaratskhelia, Ayari, Mbaye; Subs: Marquinhos, Mendes, Lucea, Vitinha, Neves, El Nay, Idder, Drame, Bourdin, Ndjantou, Meite, Longoni, Chevalier

And here’s a famous match that took place there, giving a certain Sir Alex Ferguson his first European trophy.

“Get a bit sharper, get better on the ball, go up a notch.”

“It’s not about today it’s about preparing. Some players have played 90 minutes, some have played three games, some have just come back. So it’s about keeping working on things we’ve been working on.”

“They’re similar to us, but have fewer senior players available . They’ve had a great time and great squad so whoever on the pitch it will be a test.”

A hugely talented player for a number of clubs, including United, who ever really lived up to his early promise.

Good to have you back, lads 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/3EgkXLqcQm

I expect they’ll make an appearence at some point.

Ready to face PSG in our latest pre-season test ✊

Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

#2158. Sheffield Wednesday team news and predicted XI as Dave Challinor takes charge vs Oldham Athletic

Sheffield Wednesday travel to the North West for their first game under Dave Challinor‘s management. An FA Cup first round clash against Oldham Athletic awaits SWFC, and the new boss will be eager to make a winning start.

Challinor is tasked with turning around some poor form of late as the Owls have gone four without a win, including consecutive draws under Matt Hamshaw’s temporary lead. Wednesday have a good history in this prestigious competition though, with 2021/22 the last time they got knocked out in the first round.

Oldham Athletic meanwhile sit 18th in League Two, so will be hoping for some cup joy. In their last game, Micky Mellon’s Latics won 1-0 against Northampton Town thanks to a second-half goal from Ollie Norburn.

Challinor has a handful of injury issues to deal with as he prepares to make his Sheffield Wednesday bow. Before the game, the new boss confirmed the Owls will be without Liam Cooper, Joe Lumley and Ali Al-Hamadi as their recent absences continue.

Cooper is a precautionary call, while Lumley and Al-Hamadi are expected to step up their returns next week.

Elsewhere, Billy Mitchell and Reece James are set to miss out, as are long-term absentees Louie Barry and Tyler Onynago. Sil Swinkels is suspended after his sending off against Blackpool, but Jamal Lowe will be available for selection having served his ban.

In better news, Di’Shon Bernard has been deemed fit to return for SWFC. Challinor is wary that his minutes still need to be managed but the former Manchester United youngster’s availability serves as a welcome boost.

Centre-back Ricardo Santos returned off the bench against Blackpool and is set to be in contention again.

Maynard-Brewer; Bernard, Santos, Weaver; Valery, Heskey, Bannan, Lowe; Slattery, Keillor-Dunn; Burstow

Challinor has mainly played with a 3-4-2-1 in his managerial career to date, so that is what formation is anticipated in his first Sheffield Wednesday game. However, he has used varied three-back setups as well as a 4-2-3-1 in the past.

Lumley’s absence means Ashley Maynard-Brewer continues in goal. He will be guarded by Ernie Weaver, and the fit-again Bernard and Santos in the back three with Yan Valery and Max Lowe selected as right and left wing-backs.

The fairly limited midfield depth means SWFC will likely persist with Barry Bannan and Jaden Heskey in the middle. Callum Slattery continues in a more advanced role alongside Davis Keillor-Dunn, who has now scored four goals in 10 games for the club.

Mason Burstow continues at striker despite Lowe’s return. The experienced striker will be hoping to impact the game off the bench though, alongside the likes of Sean Fusire, Jordi Liongola, Kieran Morrison and Harry Gray.

Oldham Athletic vs Sheffield Wednesday kicks off at 17:15 on Sunday evening and will be broadcast on TNT Sports 1.

#2157. Sabatini: “Il Napoli ha giocato le tre partite più spettacolari della stagione”

Il giornalista Sandro Sabatini, attraverso un video pubblicato sul proprio canale YouTube, ha analizzato il pareggio per 1-1 tra Napoli e Lazio: “Le tre partite più belle, spettacolari, ricche di gol, emozioni e occasioni di questa stagione sono state Inter-Napoli 3-2, Napoli-Roma 3-3 e Napoli-Lazio 1-1. Il calcio dominante, propositivo e moderno si è visto in queste tre partite del Napoli, che sono state tra le migliori di un campionato che, magari dopo la sosta, potrà riservare qualche correzione. È proprio il Napoli di Allegri ad augurarsi questa correzione, perché la classifica parla chiaro. Nonostante alcune prestazioni all’altezza della situazione, gli azzurri si ritrovano staccatissimi, intorno al decimo posto, con un divario obiettivamente incolmabile per un’eventuale lotta scudetto e quasi incolmabile persino per il quarto posto. Il calcio è così, è paradossale. Non sempre si riesce a trovare una conferma o una chiave di lettura per qualsiasi partita, a meno che non ci si voglia lasciare guidare dalle ideologie e dai commenti precostituiti, anziché dalle idee e dall’analisi. Fatta questa premessa, Napoli e Lazio hanno pareggiato 1-1 al termine di una partita molto emozionante, spettacolare e combattuta. Il primo tempo è stato maggiormente favorevole alla Lazio, che infatti lo ha concluso in vantaggio per 1-0. Nella ripresa il Napoli ha trovato il pareggio, propiziato da McTominay e Hojlund, con la complicità di Pedraza, autore dell’autogol. Gli azzurri hanno poi costruito altre occasioni, neutralizzate dal portiere. Su tutte, quella clamorosa nel duello faccia a faccia con De Bruyne. Sì, il Napoli nel secondo tempo avrebbe potuto anche vincere, ma la Lazio è una squadra solida, che merita il primo posto in classifica. Gattuso l’ha organizzata benissimo. Mi è piaciuto tantissimo il primo tempo della Lazio, ma anche la gestione degli ultimi dieci minuti, nei quali ha giocato da grande squadra. Bisogna considerare che anche la Lazio, così come il Napoli, ha dovuto fare i conti con assenze importanti. A un certo punto è stata costretta a rinunciare a Sutalo e Nuno Tavares, oltre a dover fare a meno di Zaccagni. Tre assenze pesanti, eppure la Lazio esce dal Maradona tra la soddisfazione dei propri tifosi. I sostenitori della Lazio di Gattuso festeggiano, ed è giusto che sia così. Quelli del Napoli di Allegri, invece, se la prendono con tutti, a cominciare dall’allenatore, per arrivare a quello che sembra essere diventato l’imputato numero uno. Imputato di che cosa, poi, non si capisce bene. Pensate che Noa Lang, da un certo momento in avanti, è stato fischiato per tutta la partita. Eppure Noa Lang è stato nettamente il migliore in campo del Napoli. Un giocatore vivo, sempre pronto a puntare l’uomo. Romano Floriani Mussolini, alla sua prima presenza da titolare, ha vissuto una giornata difficilissima, tanto da essere sostituito da Lazzari, perché nessuno riusciva a fermare Lang. Eppure i tifosi del Napoli lo fischiavano. Per che cosa? Per un gesto? Per una sorta di regolamento di conti? Non si capisce. Credo sia stato qualcosa che non dovrebbe trovare spazio nel giudizio su Lang. Naturalmente i tifosi possono fare quello che vogliono, ma il rendimento di un calciatore di personalità, come lo è Lang, un folle ma dotato di personalità, non dipende certo dai fischi o dagli applausi. Il rendimento di un giocatore o di una squadra non dipende dagli applausi o dai fischi dello stadio. E la dimostrazione, per certi versi, arriva proprio dalla Lazio. Mi dispiace dirlo, perché la passione dei tifosi laziali, compresi quelli che non vanno allo stadio, è fuori discussione. Però la dimostrazione che il pubblico conta fino a un certo punto arriva proprio dalla stagione della Lazio, che gioca in uno stadio quasi deserto eppure è in testa al campionato. Una squadra che sembrava destinata a lottare per non retrocedere sta invece lottando per lo scudetto. Vedremo quali saranno gli altri risultati, ma una cosa è sicura: chi, dopo queste prime giornate e le prime due soste, esclude la Lazio dalla lotta scudetto, secondo me commette un errore. È una squadra cresciuta con Gattuso, così come è cresciuto lo stesso allenatore, tornato, secondo me, alla semplicità, alla razionalità, alla precisione, al lavoro e alla solidità del suo primo staff, senza tutte le confusioni dell’esperienza in Nazionale. Quindi complimenti alla Lazio, ma per una volta complimenti anche al Napoli. Nel Napoli, Milinkovic-Savic ha parato quello che doveva parare, poi è stato impallinato da Frattesi. Sul gol del primo tempo il pallone gli passa praticamente accanto alla faccia. Per il resto è stato preciso negli interventi. Beukema un po’ meglio rispetto alle precedenti esibizioni, anche se non ci voleva molto. Rrahmani si vede che sta tirando avanti, lottando nonostante una condizione fisica complicata e dolori che potrebbero anche metterlo in difficoltà. Eppure continua a combattere con grande leadership. Rafa Marín discreto. Aveva offerto qualcosa di meglio nel corso della stagione, ma la sua resta una prestazione sufficiente. Olivera corre più di tutti, soltanto che poi sbaglia più di tutti sotto porta. È un giocatore che, se andassimo a vedere gli xG di questo campionato, probabilmente scopriremmo essere andato vicino al gol diverse volte, anche con salvataggi sulla linea. Poverino, non riesce mai a trovare la soddisfazione della rete. Nel secondo tempo ha avuto un pallone da calciare con il destro, che non è il suo piede. Era quasi un rigore, leggermente decentrato, ma lo ha mandato oltre la traversa. McTominay molto bene nel secondo tempo, così come De Bruyne, soprattutto quando i due si sono invertiti di posizione. Gilmour geometrico, didascalico e niente più. Vergara è partito molto male, ma ha concluso meglio. A me piace anche senza i gol, perché è un giocatore che, quando troverà maggiore fiducia, autostima e leggerezza mentale, potrà diventare molto più incisivo. E poi c’è Lang. È un giocatore che può dividere. Può risultare simpatico o, più probabilmente, antipatico. Può essere considerato un professionista serio, anche se non credo sia questa l’immagine che trasmette, oppure un folle, uno scapestrato, un genialoide, un artista, un rapper. Può essere considerato tutto. Ma se i tifosi del Napoli fischiano Lang per aver fatto quel gesto, significa che la competenza calcistica viene superata dall’umore, dall’invidia o da qualcosa che non ha nulla a che fare con il calcio e, se posso permettermi, nemmeno con il sostegno di cui questa squadra ha bisogno. Lo dico per i tifosi del Napoli, ma anche per quelli dell’Inter, della Roma, per quelli che l’anno scorso contestavano le proprie squadre e per quelli della Fiorentina. Se si va allo stadio concentrandosi sul fischiare un giocatore e sul trovare un capro espiatorio, come è successo anche a Lucca nell’ultimo quarto d’ora, va bene, si può fare tutto. I tifosi ne hanno il diritto, ma l’appoggio è un’altra cosa. Ed è proprio l’appoggio che i tifosi dovrebbero dare. Per me Lang è un giocatore di livello internazionale. È ovvio che non giocherà tutte le partite come questa, ma le sue qualità non si discutono. Concludendo, la Lazio è in corsa per lo scudetto. Il Napoli, se dovesse continuare a giocare così, potrebbe tornare a lottare per un posto tra le prime quattro. Ma deve continuare su questa strada”.

#2155. Ex-Manchester United star delivers ‘unbelievable’ Rangers transfer verdict

Former Manchester United star Quinton Fortune reckons his South African countryman Olwethu Makhanya's move to Rangers has been a huge success.

The defender has won plenty of plaudits after a fine start to his Ibrox career following his £3 million summer move from MLS side Philadelphia Union.

And former Old Trafford and Atletico Madrid star Fortune believes Makhanya has flourished since his switch to Rangers. He said: "I watched Olwethu Makhanya a little bit when he was in MLS before and his transfer to Rangers has been a great move for him.

"It is unbelievable that he is able to play for Rangers in the Scottish Premiership. But that's what he had to do - go up another level.

#2154. Blackburn Rovers defender has had an excellent breakout year – but patience is required: Opinion

Blackburn Rovers have had a largely frustrating 2026, but there has been reason to believe. The return of Tony Mowbray has seen the club build on Michael O’Neill’s work and pushed the club up into mid-table.

Another huge positive over the last year has been the emergence of Tom Atcheson. The 20-year-old becoming one of Rovers’ most encouraging academy success stories, with his development over the past 12 months earning him recognition on the international stage.

His form has also attracted attention from several top clubs. Atcheson was the subject of enquiries from Manchester City, Liverpool, Chelsea, Newcastle United, Sunderland and Crystal Palace in the summer window.

The 20-year-old has progressed from a promising youngster to a regular Championship starter and an increasingly important member of Northern Ireland’s defence. His senior breakthrough has not simply been a reward for potential, either.

Consistent performances at club level have given O’Neill plenty of reasons to trust him, with Atcheson starting all four of Northern Ireland’s Nations League fixtures in September and October, helping them record a run of clean sheets.

That is a significant achievement for a player who only made his senior international debut in March. Having joined Blackburn at under-12 level, Atcheson enjoyed a loan spell with Marine before making his Championship debut against Millwall in December 2025.

14 league appearances followed last season, and he has since established himself as a regular under Tony Mowbray.

Atcheson’s underlying numbers this campaign suggest there is plenty to like, although they also highlight why expectations should remain measured. His average FotMob rating of 6.54 also indicates that, despite his impressive international progress, he has not consistently been among the Championship’s standout defenders.

There have been occasional reminders of his inexperience, too. His first international start against Guinea in June ended with a goal and a red card, while a difficult 45 minutes against Swansea last month preceded a minor groin problem that forced him to miss the subsequent Stoke fixture.

Nevertheless, Blackburn have every reason to be encouraged. Atcheson has already demonstrated that he can translate Championship reliability into international performances, and his physical profile makes him an appealing long-term prospect.

The Premier League comparisons may be premature, but his trajectory is undeniably positive. Another six to 12 months of consistent performances could take his reputation, and his market value, to another level.

#2153. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena dell'8 novembre

SASSUOLO, AQUILANI ORMAI ESONERATO. BOVE: “HO SEMPRE UN OCCHIO VERSO L’ITALIA” -   Una decisione sofferta ma ormai praticamente presa. Il futuro di Alberto Aquilani è sempre più lontano dal Sassuolo, a un passo dall’esonero. Gli ultimi risultati, 1 punto in 6 partite, hanno portato a imboccare una strada che un mese fa nessuno poteva immaginare visto il lavoro iniziato. Nemmeno lo stesso Aqullani, che anche se questa avventura finirà, resta un allenatore emergente con idee e spunti, gli stessi che aveva fatto vedere l’anno scorso nella splendida cavalcata con il Catanzaro. Un’annata con una promozione sfiorata di un soffio.

E dire che la sua prima avventura in serie A era cominciata bene, con la soddisfazione anche di una vittoria contro la Juventus e il pareggio con il Milan. Un Sassuolo con un’identità ben precisa. Dalla sconfitta con il Frosinone la squadra però non ha più saputo reagire denotando una grande fragilità, soprattutto a livello difensivo. Alla fine, come sempre, i risultati hanno fatto la differenza e portato la società ad andare verso un’altra direzione. Domani tutto sarà più chiaro con il Sassuolo che dovrà scegliere il sostituto. Tanti i nomi al vaglio del ds Palmieri: Paulo Sousa, Montella, D’Aversa e Calzona sono profili su cui si sta concentrando l’attenzione del club neroverde che nelle prossime ore farà la sua scelta definitiva.

"Ho scelto di raccontare la mia esperienza perché mi sono sentito fortunato, sono in vita e posso farlo, volevo ridare indietro l'affetto che ho ricevuto, trasformare le difficoltà in qualcosa di utile: vorrei che chiunque veda il documentario trovi energia per le proprie sfide personali, e anche il coraggio di farsi aiutare se necessario": così, parlando nel corso della puntata odierna de La Domenica Sportiva, Edoardo Bove, intervenuto nella nota trasmissione di Rai 2 per presentare il documentario "In un battito", che ripercorre la sua vita.

Segnata da un malore che ha messo a rischio la sua vita, quando era in campo. Ma è questo un ricordo passato: "Certo, gioco in maniera diversa adesso. Mi sono preparato durante questo lungo periodo al rientro in campo, sapevo che avrei trovato difficoltà a livello mentale anche nel rapporto con il mio cuore e il suo battito, a volte c'è la paura di ricordare; anche per questo è stato importante affrontare tutto, fare un percorso interiore che i aiutasse a gestire il tutto. In campo adesso sono tranquillo, ma la differenza l'ha fatta l'aver lavorato con dei professionisti che mi hanno permesso di superare tutto ciò: essere ora in Inghilterra mi rende anche felice, era comunque un sogno che avevo. Però non nascondo di avere un occhio verso l'Italia".

A tal proposito, una nota alla Roma: "Secondo me ha grandissime potenzialità, soprattutto nel campionato italiano in questo momento ha un ritmo molto elevato. Si difende attaccando, ha un gioco quasi asfissiante, a uomo: ho giocato contro Gasperini quando ero in Italia, ricordo bene il tipo di gioco e quanto mettesse in difficoltà gli avversari. Ma che è una Roma positiva non devo certo dirlo io".

Il futuro di Francesco Camarda potrebbe presto tingersi di una nuova maglia, seppur temporaneamente. Secondo quanto riportato oggi dal Corriere dello Sport, il Milan sta valutando con grande attenzione l'ipotesi di cedere in prestito il giovane centravanti durante la prossima sessione invernale di mercato, offrendogli così l'opportunità di trovare la continuità d'impiego necessaria per accelerare il suo percorso di crescita professionale.

Il classe 2008, chiuso nel ruolo di vice-Gonçalo Ramos all'interno della rosa rossonera, ha racimolato finora appena 6 presenze complessive tra campionato ed Europa League, per un minutaggio totale fermo a quota 119 minuti. Troppo poco spazio per mostrare la propria qualità, a discapito di quanto previsto inizialmente da Ruben Amorim nella scelta di tenerlo in rosa.

E quindi? La situazione di stallo ha indotto diversi club tra Serie A e Serie B a muoversi concretamente per sondare il terreno con l'entourage di Camarda, dal Frosinone al Monza, fino a Catanzaro e Pisa che si sono già informate sulla situazione del talento cresciuto nel vivaio del club di via Aldo Rossi. Sicuramente scaldare la panchina non è un'opzione per il resto della stagione.

MANCHESTER UNITED, CARRICK: “NON MI DIMETTERÒ”. MONACO, LIVERPOOL IN PRESSING PER CAMARA -  Il Manchester United continua a vivere una stagione complicatissima, ma Michael Carrick non ha alcuna intenzione di abbandonare la panchina dei Red Devils. Dopo il rocambolesco 4-4 contro l'Aston Villa, il tecnico inglese ha escluso categoricamente l'ipotesi di dimissioni, nonostante il deludente diciottesimo posto in Premier League. Interrogato sull'eventualità di lasciare il proprio incarico, Carrick ha risposto senza esitazioni ai microfoni di Sky Sports: "Non succederà".

L'allenatore, 45 anni, ha poi riconosciuto le difficoltà attraversate dalla squadra, capace di conquistare appena una vittoria nelle prime dieci giornate di campionato. "Conoscete la situazione, non abbiamo vinto abbastanza partite. Ma ho tutta l'intenzione di proseguire il lavoro che abbiamo iniziato, ripartendo dai tanti aspetti positivi mostrati oggi, correggendo alcuni errori e tornando a vincere".  Il futuro di Lamine Camara potrebbe essere lontano dal Monaco. Il centrocampista senegalese classe 2004, 22 anni, è diventato uno dei nomi più seguiti dai grandi club della Premier League, pronti a contenderselo nelle prossime sessioni di mercato. Secondo quanto riportato dal portale footy-africa.com, il Liverpool avrebbe intensificato i contatti con l'entourage del giocatore, nel tentativo di anticipare la concorrenza e capire i margini per una possibile operazione. L'interesse dei Reds rappresenta un elemento importante per il futuro del calciatore, anche se al momento non risultano accordi raggiunti con il Monaco.

Il Liverpool, tuttavia, non è l'unica società inglese sulle tracce del centrocampista. Anche Chelsea e Manchester United continuerebbero infatti a monitorarne la situazione, mantenendosi in corsa per un eventuale trasferimento. Una concorrenza che potrebbe rendere particolarmente movimentato il mercato attorno a Camara, considerato un profilo interessante per qualità tecniche, dinamismo e prospettive di crescita. Il Monaco si trova dunque a dover gestire l'attenzione crescente nei confronti di uno dei suoi giovani talenti, mentre dalla Premier League arrivano segnali di un interesse sempre più concreto. Per ora il Liverpool sembra essere il club più attivo nei contatti, ma la presenza di Chelsea e Manchester United lascia aperti diversi scenari. Il futuro di Camara potrebbe diventare uno dei temi più caldi delle prossime finestre di mercato.

#2151. Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

Considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

This has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

It’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back currently.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

What can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

They’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

#2150. Scotland's rivals reinstate under-fire duo after fake Covid certificate bans

Switzerland boss Murat Yakin insisted he never had any doubts about reinstating his captain Granit Xhaka and striker Breel Embolo to face Scotland in the Nations League.

Scotland face group leaders Switzerland in St Gallen during the latest international break, after a home game against North Macedonia.

The World Cup quarter-finalists have included veteran Sunderland star Xhaka and Atlanta United ace Embolo after they were both dumped from the previous four games in the competition following an investigation into them obtaining fake Covid certificates.

Xhaka and Embolo were handed suspended financial penalties, with Xhaka receiving a suspended fine of 150,000 Swiss francs and being placed on two years’ probation.

Ex-Celtic star tells Martin O'Neill why he's on receiving end of 'flak with love'

Celtic revival or one-off resistance and is Duran the best player in Scotland?

And Yakin insisted he never hesitated in including them in his latest squad, where they face Slovenia too. He said: "That was never up for debate for me. Granit Xhaka is our leader.

"The only problem would have been if Manu Akanji, who stood in as captain in the last four games, had wanted to remain captain. But he sees Granit as the captain.

"We have a lot of battles for a place in the squad - the competition is very fierce. We have done well in this competition so far, and a point would be enough to win the group in our next match in Maribor.

"But we want to win every game in our group and maintain our 100 per cent record."

#2149. What Alex Neil must learn from Millwall’s 3-0 defeat to West Brom heading into the international break

Millwall have had a terrible opening third of the 2026/27 season. The Lions suffered their seventh loss of the campaign and their second this week as West Brom were 3-0 victors at The Hawthorns on Saturday.

Alex Neil’s side did well to nullify a WBA side who were unbeaten in five before the weekend inside the first 45 minutes. However, the second half saw the South London outfit capitulate defensively as they made it 27 goals conceded this term.

Millwall will welcome the pause in Championship action for two weeks as they reset. There are certainly many lessons learned from their latest defeat that the Lions must use as fuel over the international break to come back stronger heading into the busy winter period.

This time last year, when Millwall headed into the international break, they were sat 6th in the table and just four points off the top two. Now after their second consecutive 3-0 loss, the Lions are 16th in the Championship and six points from the top eight.

Neil’s side have scored six more goals than they did this time last season. However, they have conceded seven more times. Saturday highlighted the gulf in quality and momentum between a side in real play-off contention like West Brom and a team in disarray like Millwall.

The Baggies had an xG of 2.98 whereas the South London outfit only had an xG of 0.62. The Lions also had just nine touches inside the opposition’s box and won just 48% of their ground duels.

All three goals Millwall conceded against West Brom weren’t entirely at the fault of the New Zealand international. However, it’s safe to say that the Lions won’t achieve anything this season with him as their number one.

Max Crocombe has conceded 22 goals this term out of 10 games and has a save percentage of 55.1%. He is currently averaging 2.2 goals conceded per match, and the 33-year-old is struggling to cope with the demands of the Championship.

Against WBA, the New Zealand international made an error leading to a goal and made just three saves. With Lukas Jensen reported to be nearing a return to fitness and his save percentage standing at 100% from his two games this term, Neil won’t select Crocombe again if he doesn’t have to.

One positive Millwall can take from the clash against West Brom is the return of duo Josh Coburn and Tairyk Arconte. Coburn played 54 minutes before being substituted, whilst Arconte featured for the last 10 minutes.

Both players have been crucial to the limited success Neil’s side has had this season. Coburn especially had a strong start to the term before an injury sidelined him for two months. He has won 69.2% of his aerial duels this campaign and has an xG on target of 3.14.

Arconte was also missed by the Lions. He has netted three times in nine games for Millwall in his debut Championship season. The 22-year-old has a successful dribble rate of 60% and has made 45 touches inside the opposition box.
