#2031. SPFL round-up: Partick Thistle go top as Hamilton stunned by Cove Rangers

Partick Thistle climbed to the top of the William Hill Championship with a 1-0 victory over rock-bottom Queen’s Park.

The moment of the game came 10 minutes after the break when Seb Drozd’s effort deflected to Tony Watt at the far post who headed Thistle to victory and climbed above Raith who drew 0-0 with Dunfermline.

Dylan Borso scored four times as they came from behind to win 4-3 and inflict a fourth straight defeat on Stenhousemuir despite playing more than an hour with a man less after Calvin Okike was sent off for the hosts.

Arbroath ended a run of five-straight defeats in style as they earned a convincing 4-1 win over Ayr courtesy of goals from Thomas O’Brien, Michael McKenna, Gavin Reilly and Jacob MacIntyre.

Cristian Montano’s equaliser cancelled out Alfie Stewart’s opener as Livingston drew 1-1 with Inverness.

In League One, Ross County moved five points clear at the top of the league after they ran out 4-1 winners over Peterhead.

Brian Graham and Chris Hamilton gave County a 2-0 lead before Mitch Megginson pulled a goal back for the visitors but the home side finished the job with further goals from Richard Chin and Kieran Phillips’ penalty.

Second-placed Hamilton suffered a shock first defeat of the season after they were thrashed 4-0 by rock-bottom Cove Rangers thanks to Edimond Oppong’s hat-trick and Joseph Teasdale’s late strike.

Goals from Jamie Hamilton and Cameron Elliott’s penalty helped East Kilbride come from behind and earn a first win four games with a 2-1 victory over Queen of the South.

Cammie Ross struck four minutes from time to give East Fife a second-straight win as they beat Montrose 2-1 who had goalscorer Blair Lyons sent off late.

Airdrieonians ended a run of three consecutive defeats with a 3-2 win over lowly Alloa courtesy of Rangers loanee Josh Gentles’ late goal.

Stranraer remained at the top of League Two with a 3-0 victory over Stirling who saw their five-match league unbeaten run come to an end.

Second-placed Clyde picked up a third win from their last four after they twice came from behind to beat The Spartans 3-2.

Leighton McIntosh and Scott Honeyman gave Dumbarton a first win in four with a 2-0 victory over Elgin.

Jack Brydon’s late strike earned Kelty Hearts a 2-1 win over Annan Athletic while Forfar drew 1-1 with Edinburgh.

#2030. Arsenal vs Hull City preview: Arteta sticks with winning formula as Gunners target another three points

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have resisted the temptation to rotate after their victory at Anfield, with Mikel Arteta naming the same starting XI for Saturday’s meeting with Hull City.

Arsenal welcome Championship side Hull City to the Emirates Stadium, looking to strengthen their grip on the top spot after collecting 24 points from their opening nine Premier League games. However, their tally of just 14 goals suggests Arteta’s side still have work to do in the final third.

Arteta has again chosen to partner Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães in defence. William Saliba was left out despite pre-match talk that he would be named in the starting XI. Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman are also missing from the squad.

Noni Madueke will carry the right. Tzolis starts on the opposite flank. Kai Havertz will lead the line. Viktor Gyökeres, Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino add attacking options from the bench.

Arsenal predicted starting XI: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimarães, Rice, Ødegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Hincapié, Lewis-Skelly, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Gyökeres.

Hull are coming into this game ranked 11th in the league after five draws in their first nine games. They’ve not won in their last eight games but can cause problems for any opposition.

They look like playing a defensive game with Slater, Iroegbunam and Gourna-Douath in the midfield to protect the backline. McBurnie and Cho will give them some attacking options.

Hull starting XI: Tzolakis; Coyle, Ajayi, Egan, Mendy, Stroud; Slater, Iroegbunam, Gourna-Douath; McBurnie, Cho.

Substitutes: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Gelhardt, Hjerto-Dahl, Norton-Cuffy, Herrington, Mouzakitis, Vaz.

McBurnie is just one booking away from suspension for the clash against Brighton on November 22 but may make an important impact in the physical battle with Gabriel.

Hull have not scored at the Emirates since 2014 but will look to turn that around. However, their main concern will be to ensure they keep Arsenal quiet for as long as possible.

Arsenal will need to find ways to break down the likely tight Hull backline.

Ødegaard and Rice will be key in keeping possession and creating chances, whilst Madueke and Tzolis will create width and movement.

Hull may be exposed to threat in case they are trapped in defence for too long, but Arteta can use Gyökeres if Havertz is having difficulties doing anything productive.

A win for Arsenal will give them a six-point lead. Manchester City will be looking to get all three points when they face Nottingham Forest later on Saturday.

The visitors will look to create an uncomfortable afternoon for the Gunners.

Arsenal have enough quality to take all three points, but Hull will not make it easy for them. I expect this to be a tight game, and the Gunners will win by a small margin.

#2029. Player Ratings: Blackburn 2-1 West Ham as Hermansen Has a Nightmare

West Ham’s promising start at Ewood Park ultimately counted for very little as Scott Parker’s side slipped to a 2-1 defeat against Blackburn Rovers. Despite enjoying plenty of possession and creating opportunities, the Hammers were undone by poor defending and some particularly questionable goalkeeping.

Joël Piroe’s late goal gave West Ham a chance of rescuing something, but the longer the game went on, the worse we seemed to play. There were some decent individual performances, particularly early on, but others will want to forget this afternoon in a hurry.

A really poor afternoon for the goalkeeper. I thought he could have been far more commanding for Blackburn’s opening goal, whether that meant catching the cross, punching it or simply getting something on the ball. He did make a straightforward late save from Todd Cantwell, but that doesn’t change my overall assessment.

One of West Ham’s more reliable performers before being substituted. Made some useful defensive interceptions and regularly pushed forward to support Bowen down the right. Tried a couple of long throws into the penalty area, although they didn’t really cause Blackburn much trouble.

Had some positive moments going forward, including a driving run from defence and a header that went narrowly wide early in the second half. However, I thought he could have done better for Blackburn’s first goal, and his performance deteriorated badly towards the end. Was fortunate not to concede a penalty before slipping twice during a dreadful passage of play that handed Blackburn a dangerous counter-attack.

Probably West Ham’s most dependable defender on the day. Made several important interceptions, particularly down the left where Blackburn repeatedly threatened, and was willing to carry the ball forward to help build attacks. Also produced a decent cross for Castellanos, although the resulting header went wide.

A mixed afternoon for the youngster. I was impressed with his willingness to get forward, his passing combinations with Austbø and some of the crosses he delivered. However, Blackburn repeatedly targeted his side, often leaving him facing two opponents, and he was beaten too easily in the build-up to the opening goal. Still very much learning the position.

Didn’t think he had a particularly good game. Had plenty of involvement, took the corners and got himself into shooting positions, but too often the final product was disappointing. Lost possession unnecessarily on occasions, failed to close down Blackburn’s second goalscorer quickly enough and wasted a promising late free kick with poor delivery.

You certainly couldn’t fault his work rate. At times he seemed to be everywhere, covering at left-back, appearing on the right and getting forward to support the attack. However, he wasn’t nearly as influential on the ball as he had been during the second half against Cardiff, and his shooting was disappointing. Replaced by Castellanos after 64 minutes.

One of West Ham’s more inventive players, particularly during the first half. Looked to move the ball quickly, attempted some clever through passes and wasn’t afraid to shoot, forcing one save and seeing another effort deflected behind. Not everything worked, but at least he was trying to make things happen.

I was genuinely surprised when he was substituted because he’d been one of West Ham’s livelier attacking players. Produced a lovely dribble past two defenders in the first half, linked up well with Mayers and delivered an excellent cross that Bowen headed against the post. Could perhaps have offered Mayers more defensive protection before Blackburn’s opener, but I thought he was contributing plenty going forward.

Blackburn 2-1 West Ham: Austbo was one of the Hammers better players

Worked hard to make things happen and was heavily involved in West Ham’s attacking play, particularly from the right. Unlucky to see his header strike the post following Austbø’s cross, while a difficult chance from close range went wide as he was falling and sliding. Also produced a lovely chipped delivery for Souček’s late header, but couldn’t quite provide the decisive contribution West Ham needed.

A frustrating performance rescued to some extent by an excellent goal. Too often he seemed hesitant in promising positions, allowing defenders to recover, while one particularly poor pass in the second half wasted a good attacking opportunity. However, he reacted brilliantly to Castellanos’ cross in the 82nd minute, firing high into the roof of the net. Whatever else you say about his performance, he took that chance extremely well.

Replaced Austbø after 58 minutes and was practically anonymous. Considering how involved Austbø had been, the substitution certainly didn’t improve West Ham’s attacking threat down the left.

Introduced for Kanté after 64 minutes and provided the cross that led to Piroe’s goal. Also had a header go wide from a Kilman delivery and was involved in the scramble that presented Bowen with a difficult chance. At least contributed something tangible to the attack.

Didn’t have a great deal of time to influence proceedings, particularly with West Ham having already lost their shape. Played one very silly ball into Orford inside our own penalty area, creating unnecessary danger. However, he also got into one of those familiar goalscoring positions in stoppage time, only to direct his header straight at the goalkeeper from Bowen’s excellent delivery.

Another substitute who came into a team that had lost its shape and was struggling for confidence. Was put in a difficult position by Souček’s poor pass inside the penalty area and was fortunate not to concede a penalty. Difficult to judge him too harshly given the limited time he had on the pitch and the state of the game when he entered.

#2028. Arsenal 1-0 Hull City: Martin Ødegaard rescues Gunners with late winner at the Emirates

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal needed a moment of quality from their captain to overcome Hull City and claim a narrow 1-0 Premier League victory at the Emirates Stadium.

Martin Ødegaard scored in the 72nd minute as the hosts struggled to break down a resolute Hull side. It was much like I expected in my match preview, as Arsenal had to work hard to win this game.

The result gives them an extended lead at the top of the table. Ahead of Manchester City’s clash with Nottingham Forest. However, Mikel Arteta will be aware that his team did not play well in this game. It was far from a walk in the park.

Hull arrived at London looking to play an attacking game. Jakirovic’s side were well organised and looked to launch quick counter attacks.

They did have some positive moments in the first half, but Arsenal struggled to get into their attacking rhythm. Kai Havertz couldn’t capitalise on one good chance created by Ødegaard.

The hosts were hopeful of taking the lead after Havertz fell to the ground in the box after being pulled back by Nobel Mendy.

However, referee Farai Hallam’s initial decision was overturned after a VAR review showed Havertz was offside earlier in the attack, so Arsenal’s penalty was cancelled.

Another frustrating moment for the home side, who failed to score during the first half, despite dominating possession.

Arsenal came out strong after the break. However, Hull were still causing problems. Lewie Coyle was also walking a fine line after a yellow card in the first half and a late challenge on Christos Tzolis.

Arteta made a three-man change on the hour mark, bringing on Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino for Havertz and Declan Rice. Six minutes later he brought on Eberechi Eze and Piero Hincapié.

The breakthrough came from Madueke, forcing Konstantinos Tzolakis into action. The Hull keeper couldn’t hold his shot, and Ødegaard was quickest to react, scoring from the rebound.

The captain’s strike took the frustration out of Arsenal’s efforts and was a reward for their perseverance. It also provided another vital moment for the Norwegian. He’s had a tough campaign so far due to injuries.

Despite going behind, Hull never gave up in their search for an equaliser. However, Arsenal held on to their lead.

Arsenal dominated the game with 67% of possession and 21 shots, compared to just seven for Hull. Tzolakis put in a number of key interventions to keep the scoreline respectable.

Although they weren’t at their best, Arsenal were able to perform in the key moments of the game. Ødegaard’s goal meant that the Gunners earned three points and are sitting top of the Premier League heading into the international break.

#2027. Blackburn Rovers 2- 1 West Ham | Boos and ironic cheers highlight massive concern

THERE was an ironic cheer from the West Ham away supporters at about 88 minutes, which considering their team was 2- 1 down and looking clueless was even more remarkable.

The cheer was for Mads Hermansen finally making a save, with a shot hit straight at him being pretty much the first time he’d connected with anything, as another two goals had found their way under and past the hapless Dane.

7000 West Ham fans had made the trip to Blackburn in expectation of a triumphant start to Parker’s era and yet saw their starting eleven dominate the ball but fail to score. Hermansen had dealt with a smattering of booing from his own fans ever since Rovers took the lead with a header that went between the Dane’s legs.

Times’ up, Mads. The big concern was that Scott Parker picked him ahead of Areola. We told him….

Hardly a confidence boost for the young keeper who surely should not have been selected in the first place.

No criticism through could be attached to Hermansen for Blackburn’s second goal but West Ham found themselves two goals behind, chasing the game and seemingly nothing to offer, back passing and fiddling around in the last few minutes.

#2026. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#2025. Europa League preview: AC Milan vs. Ferencvaros – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan are back in front of their own fans on Thursday night, hoping to correct their European course against Ferencvaros.

Milan are buoyed by the derby win over Inter at the weekend, and yet in continental competition they have struggled so far having lost two of three. So, the pressure remains on to bounce back and start climbing the Europa League table before it is too late.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In his pre-match press conference, Ruben Amorim admitted that his side needed to find some consistency, especially after the win against Inter. Effectively, his message was that the win would mean little if it wasn’t followed with another three points.

Game date: Thursday, November 4 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Urs Schnyder (VAR: Fähndrich)

As mentioned above, Milan could hardly be going into this game feeling any better after they scored three first-half goals to down their city rivals for a fourth straight time. Christian Pulisic, Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira scored in a 3-1 win that was well engineered by Ruben Amorim.

The Rossoneri continue to demonstrate their potential domestically, even if they remain seven points off top, but in the Europa League things haven’t gone to plan. Losses to Benfica and Bournemouth – both without scoring – either side of the rout of RB Salzburg leave them on three points from three games.

That puts Milan in 24th place in the table on goals scored, which is the final play-off spot. So, a big improvement is needed in the final five games of the league phase in order for the tag of being among the pre-tournament favourites to be justified.

Mario Gila, Rabiot and Moreira all returned to the line-up against Inter, which provided a very noticeable boost. However, there are no new recoveries in view of the match against Ferencvaros, so the depth is still limited.

Fikayo Tomori is in the treatment room after suffering a torn muscle in his right thigh, joining Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze who also remain out. The latter may yet require surgery on a hip issue.

The other major absentee is Mike Maignan, who saw red for shoving Tyler Adams in the face during the last Europa League game against Bournemouth and will be forced to serve a one-match ban, which is less than feared.

The latest from the various media reports suggests that Amorim will field quite a youthful side, as he has done in Europe so far. This means chances should be given to Lorenzo Torriani, Sankhoun Diawara, Ardon Jashari, Davide Bartesaghi, Omari Hutchinson, Alphadjo Cisse and potentially more.

Expectations about rotation seem likely to be proven right, with the defence being almost completely changed. Without a back-up, Torriani is indeed given the nod.

Then, the backline is made of a largely rotated group. Filippo Terracciano will start at right-back, whilst Koni De Winter will partner Diawara in the middle of the back four. Bartesaghi returns at left-back.

In midfield, Hutchinson and Cisse will start on the flanks as expected, with Yunus Musah and Jashari given the nod in the middle of the park.

Despite suggestions that Camarda could start, it seems Goncalo Ramos will be given the starting role again.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Comotto, Modric, Moreira, Pulisic, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Maignan, Pavlovic, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze, Gabbia, Tomori, Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano.

Ferencvaros went into last season as defending league champions under head coach Robbie Keane, but were forced to settle for second place. They did win the domestic cup though, and got to the last-16 of the Europa League before being beaten by Braga.

Keane left before the 2026-27 campaign, and he was replaced by Balazs Borbely who came from Gyor ETO, the club that have been one of the surprise packages in recent years, even winning the Nemzeti Bajnokság I (league title) last season.

It was quite a quiet summer for the Budapest-based team, as their big splash was Veljko Birmancevic from Sparta Praha for €2m. Matus Bero and Nathan Zohore arrived on free transfers, while Adam Nagy joined for a low fee from Spezia.

There were a few more exits though: Elton Acolatse, Zsombor Gruber, Mohammed Abu Fani, Gabi Kanichowsky and Cebrail Makreckis all left for figures between €2.5m and €1m, while five departed on free transfers too.

It has been a good start for Borbely, given that Ferencvaros are undefeated in their last 20 matches across all competitions, and they are dreaming of securing direct qualification to the last-16 of the competition.

The Zöldek have three wins from three, occupying fourth place in the overall standings behind Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen and Bournemouth. To qualify for the group stage, they overcame Twente, Gornik Zabrze and Trabzonspor, beating the latter 5-0 on aggregate.

An away win against Celtic kicked off their league phase, following by victories against Viktoria Plzen and Torreense. Overall, the Hungarian outfit have scored nine times and have conceded just three in what has been a perfect start in the UEL.

Ferencvaros’ only defeat came in their league debut on July 26 (2-4 against Baksi FC). Since then, they have gone on a long unbeaten streak of five wins and five draws, climbing to third place, just two points behind league leaders Gyor and with a game in hand.

In terms of injury news, the visitors will be missing Slovakian midfielder Matus Bero, while Bence Otvos is recovering from an ACL injury and will not take part. Aside from that, they have a clean bill of health.

Borbely’s side have so far alternated between a 4-1-4-1 formation – deploying former Liverpool player Nabi Keita or Adamy Nagy (who played for Bologna and Spezia) as midfielders – and a 4-2-3-1 to offer a bit more width.

A few rotations are expected from the weekend’s game – where they cruised to a 2-0 win – and the first set comes in defence. Radnoti, Nagy, Zohore and O’Dowda are all expected to return to the starting XI, with Gomez being the only survivor to retain his place.

Maiga will find a new partner at the base of the midfield in the aforementioned Nagy, whilst Zachariassen will start ahead of them.

On the wings, it’s an unchanged set-up with leading goalscorer Zachariassen and Birmancevic starting. Then, Yusuf is expected to return to the starting XI.

Predicted Ferencvaros XI (4-2-3-1): Radnoti; O. Nagy, Zohore, Gomez, O’Dowda; Maiga, A. Nagy; Arzani, Zachariassen, Birmancevic; Yusuf.

Predicted bench: A Varga, Dibusz, Osvath, Raemaekers, Cadu, Madrasz, Corbu, Bamidele, Bero, Joseph, Levi, Arzani, Rommens, Pappoe, Z Varga, Keita.

This will be the first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros, making it a historic encounter as a result.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match. Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencáros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026/2027.

➤ AC Milan will look to build on their derby success when they welcome an unbeaten Ferencváros side to the Stadio Giuseppe Meazza in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday evening. Ruben Amorim’s team have enjoyed a promising domestic campaign but struggled to replicate that form in Europe, occupying 24th place in the league-phase standings with just three points from their opening three matches. Their Hungarian opponents, meanwhile, sit fourth with a perfect nine-point return and arrive in Italy chasing a fourth consecutive European victory.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter Milan at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing. They suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11. Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures. Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967/68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level. Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

Sankhoun Diawara has been superb so far when called upon, and he’ll replace the ever-present Strahinja Pavlovic here. A big performance would not only reassure the club of his ability (and potential), but it may offer a reason to change January plans.

It feels like a weekly occurrence now, but Goncalo Ramos needs a goal. If Francesco Camarda is not going to start here, the Portuguese needs to prove that there is reason to keep the youngster on the bench. For his sake, as much as the Italian’s.

For the visitors, Kristoffer Zachariassen is the main danger man. Contributing to 11 goals in 21 games so far this season, the 32-year-old will be essential to Ferencvaros getting anything on Thursday.

Then, Mariano Gomez will represent a difficult opponent for whoever leads the Rossoneri’s line. The Argentine defender has been excellent so far this season, and it’s entirely possible that he contributes to a frustrating night.

Despite their rotations, Milan must win here; if they don’t, they’ll wave their Europa League top eight wishes goodbye. There’s enough quality in the starting XI to provide three points, so that will be the expectation.

#2024. West Ham Go Full Circle as Blackburn Expose Familiar Problems

West Ham’s 2-1 defeat against Blackburn Rovers was a particularly frustrating result because, for large periods of the game, Scott Parker’s side appeared to be the better team. We started brightly, enjoyed plenty of possession and created opportunities, yet somehow managed to leave Ewood Park with nothing.

What concerns me most isn’t necessarily the result itself, although that’s bad enough. It’s the manner in which West Ham gradually deteriorated as the afternoon progressed. Even after Joël Piroe pulled a goal back late on, I thought we looked increasingly disorganised and short of confidence.

And that’s perhaps the strangest aspect of Parker’s first two matches. We started against Cardiff looking completely devoid of confidence, rediscovered it during that extraordinary second-half comeback, began confidently against Blackburn and somehow finished looking just as nervous as we had before.

I was actually quite encouraged by the opening stages. West Ham pressed high, moved the ball around reasonably well and looked determined to take the game to Blackburn. Max Kilman was particularly proactive, stepping out of defence to offer an additional passing option, while Divine Mukasa and Arne Engels were regularly involved in midfield.

Down the left, Ezra Mayers and Edvin Austbø developed a promising partnership. Mayers was willing to get forward and Austbø looked lively, producing one lovely piece of skill to beat two Blackburn players before delivering a dangerous cross.

Blackburn 2-1 West Ham: Austbo was one of the Hammers better players

However, there was a problem developing on that side of the pitch. Blackburn repeatedly managed to isolate Mayers against two opponents, and while the youngster was doing some good things offensively, he wasn’t receiving enough protection defensively.

Joël Piroe was also struggling to make the most of promising situations. On one occasion, he found himself with only a single defender to beat but hesitated for so long that three opponents eventually surrounded him. West Ham were having plenty of the ball, but Blackburn were defending deeply and making it difficult to create clear opportunities.

The second half initially offered more encouragement. Mavropanos headed narrowly wide from an Engels corner, Piroe had an effort saved and then Austbø produced an excellent cross which Bowen headed against the post. At that stage, West Ham were piling on the pressure and Blackburn were struggling to get out of their own half.

Then came the sucker punch. In the 54th minute, Blackburn broke down their right, with Mayers unable to stop the delivery into the penalty area. Andri Guðjohnsen converted, but I thought several West Ham players could have done better.

Austbø might have provided more protection for Mayers, Mavropanos could have defended the situation better and I certainly felt Mads Hermansen should have been more commanding. Whether he caught the cross, punched it or simply got something on the ball, I thought the goalkeeper had an opportunity to intervene.

It was a horrible goal to concede, particularly given how much of the attacking West Ham had been doing. Parker responded by introducing Manor Solomon for Austbø, a substitution I found surprising. The Norwegian had been one of our more involved attacking players, while Solomon subsequently struggled to make any impression.

Mohamadou Kanté was then replaced by Taty Castellanos, but West Ham were finding it increasingly difficult to establish the same attacking rhythm. Blackburn’s second goal arrived in the 71st minute, with Afolayan producing an excellent finish.

Kilman had gone down following contact to his face, but too many West Ham players appeared more interested in appealing for a foul than dealing with the danger. Engels, in particular, could have done more to close down the shot. Whatever the circumstances, you cannot simply stop defending because you believe the referee should have awarded a free kick.

At 2-0, the game appeared to be slipping away, but West Ham eventually found a route back through something remarkably straightforward. Castellanos got down the right-hand side and delivered a dangerous ball into the penalty area. Piroe reacted quickly and fired high into the roof of the net in the 82nd minute.

It was an excellent finish from a striker who, in truth, hadn’t been having a particularly good afternoon. But sometimes football really is that simple. Get the ball wide, get down the line and deliver something dangerous into the box. Give your centre-forward an opportunity to attack the ball.

Suddenly it was Blackburn 2-1 West Ham, with enough time remaining to rescue a point. Unfortunately, the expected late onslaught never really materialised. In fact, I thought West Ham became progressively worse.

Mavropanos endured a dreadful few minutes, fortunate not to concede a penalty before slipping and gifting Blackburn a counter-attack. He then slipped again while attempting to recover, while Souček subsequently played a very poor pass into Lewis Orford inside our own penalty area, creating another potentially disastrous situation.

West Ham looked increasingly nervous, and the defensive organisation seemed to disappear. There were still opportunities at both ends in stoppage time, with Todd Cantwell shooting straight at Hermansen when Blackburn might have made it 3-1.

Souček then headed directly at the Blackburn goalkeeper following an excellent chipped delivery from Bowen. It was precisely the sort of position from which we’ve seen Souček score numerous times, but once again West Ham had failed to make the most of a promising opportunity.

I keep coming back to the confidence issue because I think it explains an awful lot about what we’ve witnessed over these two matches. Against Cardiff, West Ham were absolutely dreadful during the opening 45 minutes, before producing a transformation after half-time that was almost impossible to believe.

Suddenly the players looked confident, aggressive and capable of playing some very good football. That improvement appeared to carry into the opening stages at Ewood Park, where we pressed Blackburn, moved the ball with purpose and looked considerably more comfortable in possession.

Yet by the closing stages, the confidence had completely evaporated. It was almost as though we’d gone full circle in the space of two matches, ending up precisely where we started. That is particularly disappointing because I still believe this West Ham squad possesses considerably more ability than recent performances suggest.

There were some positives. Mukasa showed invention, Austbø looked dangerous, Kilman had a decent game and Piroe took his goal extremely well. But the defensive mistakes, poor decision-making and increasingly nervous football were all too familiar.

I don’t think Scott Parker can be held responsible for everything we’ve witnessed this week. He’s barely had any meaningful time on the training pitch, and the international break offers him an opportunity to start properly implementing his ideas.

However, the evidence of these two games suggests that restoring confidence isn’t simply a matter of delivering one rousing team talk. The psychological side of West Ham’s problems may be every bit as important as the tactical side.

The frustrating thing is that we’ve already seen how much better these players can perform when they believe in themselves. Against Blackburn, we watched that belief gradually disappear again.

#2023. After being benched for Celtic loan star, my on-field response was emphatic

Lucas Clearie has issued another reminder of his goalscoring potential after hitting a first-half hat-trick for Celtic B.

The 17-year-old was benched for the midweek KDM Evolution Trophy clash with Ross County, with Shim Mheuka preferred through the middle.

But Clearie responded in emphatic fashion just four days later with a first-half hat-trick against Beith Juniors. The striker opened the scoring in the 18th minute before adding another in the 42nd minute. He completed his hat-trick in the 45th minute.

His latest haul takes Clearie to an impressive 23 goals across Lowland League and KDM Evolution Trophy football this season.

Eighteen of those have arrived in the league, while he has also struck five times in four KDM Evolution Trophy outings. It was Clearie’s second hat-trick of the campaign after he previously scored three in a dramatic 4-3 victory over Stranraer.

Martin O’Neill answers Celtic ‘chucked it’ claims after major team gamble

The ongoing Celtic problem that must be ‘addressed’ in January

Chris Sutton delivers brutal ‘all-inclusive holiday’ jibe at new Celtic star

His prolific form comes as he attempts to force his way into the thoughts of first-team manager Martin O’Neill.

Clearie was among seven Celtic youngsters handed their first professional contracts in the summer of 2025 and has continued to enhance his reputation with the B team.

The teenager’s latest treble also rounded off an impressive week after he was included alongside Celtic teammate Corey Shaw in the Scotland Under-19 squad.

Scotland are due to face Kazakhstan, Kosovo and Belgium during the international window.

#2022. Chickens come home to roost as the same pairing are exposed again.. and again.. West Ham News

West Ham United will have to make do without one of their – ahem – key players when the Championship resumes after the international break. Following on from today’s 2-1 defeat against a modest Blackburn Rovers side who knew exactly what they were about this afternoon, the Hammers go into a two week period of ‘deep reflection’ before restarting against Preston North End in two weeks time.

And they’ll have to do so without £4 million – oops that should read £40 million man Maximilian Kilman who picked up a fifth yellow card of the campaign – this one apparently for simulation after being smacked cleanly in the head –  and he will therefore sit out the first game back after the merciful lull in West Ham’s shambolic descent from the top end  of the table..

In depressing echoes of a year ago, West Ham still have to set up repeatedly with Kilman and Mavropanos as the defensive pairing of doom – only a matter of time before one, or other of them is caught hopelessly out of position.

At least Dinos Mavropanos offers a goal threat – whilst when paired with Kilman is made to look defensively distinctly ordinary

In what can only be seen as a massive mistake, West Ham chose not to add to their centre back keystone cops double act in the summer window, letting Todibo leave on loan and therefore both committing and condemning themselves to the duo for the foreseeable future.

West Ham solved the problem last year – but not the number of points lost – by bringing in Axel Disasi in the January window and you’d expect them to make a similar move for an urgent upgrade this winter. Too little, too late, much as it was a year ago.

We can only hope that Airidas Golambeckis impresses enough in his outing alongside Dinos in two weeks’ time that he keeps Kilman out of the side.

To be honest, it is tough watching the same pairing year after year making the same mistakes and costing clean sheet after clean sheet. Having a goalkeeper with the arms of a five year old doesn’t help but until West Ham wake up, smell the coffee and realise that Mavropanos and Kilman will never be more than mediocre, the same results will flow, week in, week out.

#2021. Milan Futuro 2-1 Piacenza: Rossoneri move up to third in Serie D in rescheduled fixture

Today, the Milan Futuro side caught up in the fixture list, with their postponed game against Piacenza, originally scheduled for Matchday 5.

After their win last week, Milan were looking to make it two in a row and four unbeaten today, in the second half of their game against Piacenza, and they did. A 2-1 scoreline, the young Rossoneri have now moved up to third, overtaking today’s opponents.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Casting your minds back to the first half of the game on October 14, the Rossoneri were probably the weaker team. However, it was postponed due to an injury suffered by the referee, Prencipe.

The ‘second half’, then, started strongly for Navarro’s side, as they took the lead within the first five minutes. A well-orchestrated move finished by Lorenzo Ossola, and a brilliant start to the game.

It wasn’t all the Diavolo, though, and the visitors put a lot of pressure on the game, especially on the counter-attack. However, Milan held on and eventually doubled their lead in the 66th minute, thanks to Silvano Vos.

Things almost got nervy when Piacenza got one back from a set-piece, and a tense ending was set up. However, the scoreline remained the same and the Futuro took all three points.

#2020. St Johnstone boss banishes Dundee demons with ‘bitter’ declaration

Simo Valakari was thrilled to give St Johnstone supporters a 2-1 victory over Dundee to celebrate after recent Perth struggles against their Tayside rivals.

Dundee won twice at McDiarmid Park in 2024-25, the season Saints were relegated, but a transformed team has returned to the top flight under Valakari.

They drew level on 17 points with Dundee in the William Hill Premiership thanks to a fourth win of the season. Valakari lapped up the success, with fans joyous at a first home victory over the Dark Blues since October 2021.

“We are a totally new team and it is not good to hold on to all those memories,” said Valakari. “Me as a manager, of course I remember. At Christmas-time we were 3-0 down after 20 minutes of the biggest game of the season.

“And of course I remember when their fans were on the pitch celebrating on the last day. But my players don’t have this baggage. We are creating new experiences together; this is our new adventure.

“If I carried everything that happened in the past with me, I would be a very bitter person! You need to let things go; that’s why we didn’t even bring it up.

“But all the players knew how much this game meant to our fans. We needed to perform, and we did. And to perform the way we did against a very good team made it a deserved win.”

Josh Campbell headed Saints in front after five minutes before substitute Joe Westley replied early in the second half following a mix-up between goalkeeper Ross Sinclair and Cheick Diabate. Kai Fotheringham, on his first Premiership start for Saints, netted a deflected winner in the 72nd minute.

“We were very good in the first half,” said Valakari. “They changed things at half-time. It took us a bit of time to adjust and we conceded a goal in that period.

“My team showed their character and personality again. We got control back and it got better and better from that.”

Dundee manager Steven Pressley conceded that his team failed to match much of their early-season form. He admitted St Johnstone were deserving winners over the course of the match.

“Over the course of the 90 minutes, St Johnstone were probably deserving of the victory,” he said. “We didn’t quite reach the heights and the standards that we’ve set.

“It’s not a criticism, it’s just these players continuously produced really high performances and have set some incredible standards. We were just a little bit below them on some of the things that we pride ourselves on.

“And, on the things we pride ourselves on, I thought St Johnstone were very strong. We’re disappointed to go into an international break on a defeat.”

#2019. Sky: Predicted Milan XI vs. Ferencvaros – rotation galore for Amorim at San Siro

After the game against Inter, AC Milan were expected to rotate and they certainly have, based on the predicted XI to face Ferencvaros.

A win like the one against Inter takes a lot out of players, that is without considering the October which they’ve had, too. So, the standard rotation in the Europa League was expected to be increased, with reports suggesting a four-year drop in the team’s average age.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The starting XI is expected to have a very youthful feel, which most hoped would be the case in midweek games anyway. Nevertheless, it’s not a ‘throwaway’ game; it’s just as important to Ruben Amorim as the derby.

So, the changes start in defence, where Lorenzo Torriani replaces the suspended Mike Maignan, as Sky reports (seen below). Koni De Winter should be the only player to retain a starting spot in the backline, with Filippo Terracciano and Davide Bartesaghi coming in, whilst Sankhoun Diawara drops back into the back four.

In midfield, Yunus Musah will partner Ardon Jashari and they will be supported by Adrien Rabiot, who will sit ahead of the younger duo.

A vaguely youthful front line sees Omari Hutchinson and Alphadjo Cisse start on the flanks, with Goncalo Ramos starting in the middle again.

Predicted Milan XI (4-4-1-1): Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Musah, Jashari, Cisse; Rabiot; Ramos

#2018. Blackburn Rovers 2- 1 West Ham United | The morning after

Scott Parker’s words at full time pretty much summed up the remainder of this Championship season for West Ham United following the side’s first away defeat of the campaign. The new manager bounce failed to materialise as his squad thew away chance after chance against their solid opponents who twice capitalised on the now-traditional lacklustre Irons’ defending.

Speaking after the game to BBC Radio London, a hoarse Hammers head coach declared :

Not only at Ewood Park, but in the 31 remaining games of this season. A six point gap between the Hammers in ninth and the league leaders is not yet insurmountable. But it is, certainly, a mountain to climb for Parker to turn West Ham’s dreadfully mediocre-looking squad into Championship contenders.

With so many leaks, it is difficult to know which hole to plug first in the slowly sinking good ship West Ham United. Goalkeeper, defence, midfield, attack – all are areas crying out for urgent post-Nuno repair.. But none are yet beyond salvage.

A tough watch – Scott Parker will have learned a lot about his West Ham squad

As many have commented, though, it’s going to be a long season.

Right now, half a season of the dour, drab, boring but solid wins for which Scott Parker received so much criticism from his time at Burnley would be pretty well received in east London.

Usually we curse the international break but I have a feeling this time around it comes as a huge relief to the manager, the squad and supporters, for very different reasons. Amongst supporters, optimism will no doubt resurface at some stage during the next fortnight as we convince ourselves that if nothing else, we have the right man for the job at the helm.

Whatever Scott Parker is getting paid, if he somehow manages to transform this group into his trademark mean, lean, tough side capable of grinding out one-nil victories week in, week out, frankly he’ll be worth every penny.
